_binsNote: The system defines four waste streams: Organic, Recyclable, Hazardous, and Residual. Hazardous is a separate category — batteries, electronics, lamps, household chemicals — which is why hazardRules exist rather than a general_waste catch-all. Identifiers stay opaque while display names, phrases, and instructions are presented in English.

bins.guidance: Food scraps, fruit peels, leaves. Processed into compost.
Clean and dry plastic, metal, paper, and glass.
Hazardous materials. Never mix with regular waste.
Waste that cannot be recycled or composted.

_hazardRulesNote: Checked before every material rule and winning outright. A battery is still metal, and a material rule would file it as recyclable — the cost of that is a fire in the collection truck, not a contaminated load. Every instruction says what to do, because 'B3' alone does not tell someone holding a vape where to put it.

hazardRules.instruction: Do not throw in regular bins. Batteries can catch fire when crushed. Place in hazardous box.
hazardRules.note: Lithium cells vent and ignite when crushed in a truck or compactor. Vapes and power banks count here too.

hazardRules.instruction: Electronics belong in hazardous waste. Place in hazardous box or take to e-waste drop-off.
hazardRules.note: E-waste leaches heavy metals; it also usually contains a cell, so it inherits the battery risk.

hazardRules.instruction: Light bulbs belong in hazardous waste. Do not break — place carefully in hazardous box.
hazardRules.note: Fluorescent and CFL tubes carry mercury vapour.

hazardRules.instruction: Pressurised aerosol can. Place in hazardous box, do not crush.
hazardRules.note: Pressurised even when it feels empty — it explodes in a compactor.

hazardRules.instruction: Chemicals belong in hazardous waste. Seal tightly, place in hazardous box.
hazardRules.note: Paint, thinner, pesticide, bleach, motor oil.

hazardRules.instruction: Medicine belongs in hazardous waste. Do not flush down the drain.
hazardRules.note: Pharmaceutical waste is hazardous and contaminates groundwater.

hazardRules.instruction: Sharp objects. Wrap securely first, then place in hazardous box.
hazardRules.note: Protects whoever handles the waste downstream.

_componentRulesNote: Only for items whose parts genuinely go to different bins. A bottle and its cap both end up in Recyclable, so splitting that would print two rows saying the same thing; it is not here. Matched on the item name with whole-token matching, using English keywords for both Foundation Models and Vision fallback tiers.

componentRules.note: Grease disqualifies the paper stream but only touches the base. Answering 'residu' for the whole box throws away a recyclable half.

parts.name: Paper cup (plastic lined)
parts.condition: Inner plastic lining cannot be separated — not recyclable paper

componentRules.note: The single most common recycling contaminant worldwide: it looks like paper and is not.

parts.name: Container
parts.condition: If container is styrofoam, dispose in Residual bin

componentRules.note: Emptying the food out is what makes the container recyclable at all.

parts.name: Wrapper
parts.condition: Greased paper and plastic wrap soiled by food cannot be recycled

componentRules.note: Common takeaway case: greased paper plus an inner plastic layer, with food still in it.

_rulesNote: Priorities: 100 base, 150 material-specific override, 200 soiled, 300 declared-composite material, 400 the composite property override. Rule cmp_bonded_override deliberately omits 'materials' so it applies whatever material the model named — see its note.

rules.condition: Only if labelled compostable — regular plastic ruins compost
If rinsed first, it can go to Recyclable
rules.note: Food residue contaminates the plastic stream, but rinsing genuinely recovers it — say so.

rules.condition: If rinsed first, it can go to Recyclable

rules.note: Tissue and paper towels are almost always soiled.

rules.condition: Receipts are thermal paper, not regular paper
rules.note: Thermal receipt stock is BPA-coated and contaminates the paper stream. It was previously matched as 'paper' and sent to recycling.

rules.condition: If broken, wrap safely so sorters do not get hurt
Single-use plastic bags jam sorting machinery
Bonded materials cannot be separated by hand
rules.note: No 'materials' key on purpose, so it applies to whatever material was named. Fixes the case where a PE-lined cup reported as 'paper' with isComposite true matched clean_paper and was sent to recycling — isComposite was dead for every material except 'composite' itself. Regression test: bondedItemOverridesItsPrimaryMaterial.

_hazardKeywordHintsNote: The Vision fallback tier cannot report a hazard class the way the language model can, and a device without Apple Intelligence must still refuse to put a battery in a bin. These give that tier the same interception by keyword. English only — they match Vision's own label taxonomy, not what a person would say.
_visionKeywordHintsNote: Matched on whole tokens, never substrings, so 'can' cannot match 'toucan'. Bare one-word keywords are deliberate: Vision's taxonomy emits 'bottle' and 'can' far more often than any two-word phrase, and without them most real items matched nothing at all. Where a bare word and a specific phrase both match a label, the longer phrase wins, so 'beer bottle' lands in glass rather than plastic. English only, for the same reason as the hazard hints.
